svg.title: Thirty years of MGF: claims, challenges and black-market vials
svg.desc: Thirty years of MGF: claims, challenges and black-market vials. 1996: MGF named after a gene message found in stretched rabbit muscle. 2002: Lab study: synthetic MGF peptide boosts muscle cell growth. 2005: MGF added to anti-doping list; patent filings describe PEGylated versions. 2010: Review: no natural MGF peptide ever isolated in the body. 2012: Doping lab identifies an MGF analogue in two black-market products. 2014: Two drug companies fail to reproduce MGF's effects on muscle cells. 2014: Illicit “full-length MGF” analyzed; doping tests adapted to catch it. 2016: Short MGF fails to activate the IGF-1 receptor in lab assays. 2017: MGF variant found in confiscated vials. 2026: FDA: no human exposure data on PEG-MGF; review finds no human studies. By Feb 2027: FDA compounding advisory committee to discuss PEG-MGF.
